svg.font-family: Inter, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, "Liberation Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif
svg.title: Bootstrap single-agent operation versus normal multi-agent operation
svg.desc: Phase 1, bootstrap: the human operator, holding the admin credential, directly supervises one worker session that holds a worker credential, one lease epoch, and one assigned worktree. The worker sends claim, heartbeat, and submit commands to the Graphyard control plane, whose merge writer pushes gate-passing heads to the git remote. No operator agent, master loop, slice leads, or reviewer session exist yet, but every gate is enforced. Phase 2, normal operation: the human operator supplies goals and the human-only decisions. An optional scoped operator agent turns goals into bounded intent. The master loop, optional slice leads, and independent reviewer and proof producer sessions read ready work and gate state from Graphyard. The master dispatches to many worker sessions, each with its own credential, lease epoch, and worktree; workers submit exact commits to Graphyard and push nothing; the merge writer alone pushes the base branch. The gates and credential boundaries are the same in both phases.
svg.text: Phase 1 · Bootstrap: one worker under direct
Connects the repository and registers the merge writer’s deploy
key, creates the work item, and supervises the one worker
session directly. Holds the admin credential.
Claims one item, works in one assigned worktree under watch,
commits and submits the exact head; pushes nothing. It never
receives the operator credential or the deploy key.
No operator agent, no master loop, no slice leads, no reviewer session
yet: the human operator performs those duties. Every gate is already
Supplies goals, required decisions, and oversight. Still the
only authority for goals, requirement rewrites, escalation
resolution, manual proofs, and merge approval when automatic
Each holds its own worker credential, one lease epoch per
claimed item, and one assigned worktree per assignment. Still
untrusted: no operator, coordinator, or producer credential.
Base branch only. The merge writer pushes a trial-merged,
gate-passing head with its deploy key; workers push nothing.
Herdr hosts the master, lead, worker, and reviewer sessions and reports
their health. Graphyard enforces separation only through principals and
credentials; keeping the sessions independent is the runtime’s job.
AI agent session (one role, one credential)
Git remote and other external facts
Chip: credential, lease epoch, or assigned worktree the
Solid arrow: an authenticated command or authority
Dashed arrow: observation or health report, never authority
